themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints exploded to 4 reports THIS WEEK compared to a 0.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting either a disease outbreak, storm damage, or pest infestation affecting Upper East Side street canopy.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)
3,100% increase from baseline is one of the sharpest spikes in the dataset
Timing suggests a recent environmental trigger (disease, pest, or weather event)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about whether a specific pest or disease is affecting trees across the UES; request street-by-street tree health data
Speak with residents and tree experts about what might cause such a sudden spike and implications for neighborhood canopy loss

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 13 reports THIS WEEK versus a 3.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 259% increase (z-score: 5.02)—reflecting emerging friction around pandemic-era sidewalk seating or new restaurant expansion on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 13 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.02)
259% spike suggests recent expansion of outdoor seating or enforcement changes
Aligns with post-pandemic reopening trends but timing of spike suggests new or concentrated activity
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants or blocks are generating complaints; interview residents about noise, congestion, or quality-of-life impacts
Contact DoE and CB108 to learn if recent outdoor dining permits were issued or if enforcement shifted

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Double
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints nearly doubled to 52 reports LAST WEEK compared to a 24.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 114% increase (z-score: 5.32)—indicating a surge in filth, waste, or sanitation issues across the district.
evidence: 52 unsanitary condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 24.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.32)
114% increase is statistically significant and sustained from prior baseline
Unsanitary conditions are already a top-10 category (370 complaints over 90 days), and this spike indicates worsening
reporting_angles: Map the 52 complaints to identify hot zones (e.g., parks, sidewalks, subway areas) and interview residents about specific issues
Contact Sanitation Department to determine if staffing, truck routes, or waste collection changed; request public health response

themes_detail.label: Animal Complaints and Dead Animals
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints peaked at 9 reports LAST WEEK versus a 2.0-complaint weekly average (350% spike, z-score: 5.72), and animal-in-park complaints hit 9 reports TWO WEEKS AGO versus 2.2 average (300% spike, z-score: 6.19)—suggesting possible wildlife disease, food source, or habitat disruption in the district.
evidence: 9 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.72, +350%)
9 animal-in-park complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.19, +300%)
Convergence of two related spikes suggests environmental or health trigger (disease, rodent boom, or encroachment)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and NYC Health + Hospitals to investigate whether there is a disease outbreak, rodent population surge, or wildlife behavior change
Interview residents and park users about where they're seeing dead animals and what species; look for patterns suggesting a specific location or park

themes_detail.label: Illegal Postings and Street Signage Damage
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked 586% THREE WEEKS AGO (6 vs. 0.9 average, z-score: 6.57), and street sign damage complaints jumped 554% TWO WEEKS AGO (9 vs. 1.4 average, z-score: 5.41)—suggesting coordinated vandalism, graffiti, or missing infrastructure enforcement in the district.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 6.57, +586%)
9 street sign damage complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.41, +554%)
Both spikes are slightly older (2-3 weeks) but remain elevated; convergence suggests environmental or enforcement issue
reporting_angles: Request illegal postings and damaged signs data from Sanitation and DoE; map to identify if clusters appear on specific avenues or blocks
Interview community about whether they've noticed increased vandalism, graffiti, or signage damage; ask if enforcement has decreased
